six_controls.name: Incoming task token allocation
six_controls.scope: Shared weighted budget, task cost forecasts, reservations before physical requests and balance-dependent output caps.

six_controls.name: Task admission and rejection
six_controls.scope: Reward times heuristic success score per predicted token, affordability, proved contradiction skip and one deferred return.

six_controls.name: Dynamic resource correction
six_controls.scope: Provider usage reconciliation, post-task online cost correction and feedback-driven generation caps, context and attempt decisions.

six_controls.name: Stop unlikely continuations
six_controls.scope: Refusal, repeated candidates, lack of objective progress and continuation value. Generation caps bound individual responses.

six_controls.name: Output economy
six_controls.scope: CPU tools, short answer formats, exact edits, bounded retrieval and at most two compact experience cards.

six_controls.name: Cost and SLA planning
six_controls.scope: Token-value queue, global 3300-second deadline and deadline-bounded API and local tools. Task latency forecasting and joint token/time ranking remain extensions.

cleanup.size_scope: Logical sizes of removed cache files and audited duplicates. Physical free-space change depends on shared hardlinks.

limitations: The final API panel contains20 development cases with one run per model/memory combination.
Memory activity was one physical injection. Its causal effect remains uncertain.
Initial forecasts transfer from earlier policies and remain model-dependent.
Success scores are hand-written heuristics. Probability calibration remains unverified.
Early stopping takes place between API calls. Negative tasks consumed7926.2 tokens in the default primary arm.
Search correctness uses frozen exact accepted spans, which can reject a longer semantically correct answer.
The global deadline has scripted regression coverage. A full55-minute soak remains unverified.
Build duration describes this host and network.
